synopsis: NRC Regulatory Guide 1.203, issued in December 2005, defines EMDAP as four elements comprising 20 steps; PIRT ranks important physical phenomena, while BEPU reports a best-estimate result with quantified uncertainty rather than stacked conservative assumptions [f7651, f7652, f14640, f14647]. EMDAP grounds model assessment in physical experiments, emphasizes highly ranked phenomena, and requires scaling, applicability justification and uncertainty treatment when extending predictions beyond the assessment matrix or physical scale [f14644, f7836, f7661, f7663]. For automatic braking, the proposed adaptation separates component-level tests from coupled full-machine tests and uses PIRT-ranked phenomena to decide which physical tests to retain; this is expert guidance, not a nuclear requirement or a framework proven for off-road braking [f7669, f14651, f7670, f8094]. Within the validated parameter hull, changes not affecting ranked phenomena may use documented simulation-only evaluation, changes affecting them should trigger targeted physical tests, and departures from the hull or new phenomena warrant full re-validation [f7912, f7913, f7918]. The safety board should distinguish aleatory from epistemic uncertainty, but the booklet did not individually verify BEPU or CSAU, and its descriptions disagree over whether the criticism of subjective PIRT ranking was peer-reviewed [f8219, f7665, f14652, f7667]. No clean case was found in which simulation accepted under the cited nuclear framework directly produced false confidence; nevertheless, nuclear assumptions and models have been revised following operating experience and accidents [f7994, f7993].
